I farm 10.1 mu, so I will not spread money everywhere the same way. My main land is still wheat-maize, because that is what I know best and what usually gives steady grain. I will keep 8.0 mu in wheat-maize and put 2.1 mu into potato. I have done this kind of split before, and around here I also watch what other growers do. I have well irrigation, so I will push fertilizer a bit rather than risk thin stands or weak ears. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer in as base plus one topdressing at jointing, water about three times if the year is normal, and aim for a solid grain yield. For summer maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, keep nitrogen a little higher because maize eats a lot, and I will not cut back too much even if fertilizer is expensive, because losing yield hurts more than spending a few more yuan. For potato, I will use improved seed potato, give it more potassium than grain crops, ridge it well, water on time, and spray more carefully because once late blight or insects get going, it gets expensive fast. I do not make big changes unless I see them work, so this year I will mostly follow what has worked on my own field and adjust a little for cost and water.
